name: Other toys/crafts (case-by-case)
anchor: EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 element-migration limits, matched per row to the EN 71-3 material category or categories the row's scope spans, taken jointly with the US ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble-element limits (mandatory under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and the Mexican NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable soluble-element limits, which state the same measured quantity; the strictest value across that family binds each cell. Total-content law (CPSIA lead, RoHS, REACH Annex XVII, Canadian SOR coating limits) is carried as disclosed companion obligations and never as a published number.
native_basis: element migration from accessible toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material, taken jointly with the ASTM F963-17 soluble and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable rows that state the same quantity. This row's scope spans all three of the Directive's material categories; the strictest of them, Category II, is published across the whole row, except for total chromium where the Mexican modelling-clay and finger-paint tier is stricter still.
native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from accessible toy material (EN 71-3, mg/kg of material) — the strictest of the three material-category limit sets this row's scope spans (Category II) is published across the whole row; a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
scope_note: Catch-all row for toys and craft items that do not fall within rows 1 to 20, and for accessible liquids, gels and sticky materials contained inside toys certified on other rows (bath-toy liquid, gel fill, bubble solution, water-bead and slime fill, cap-firing percussion caps). Because the material form is not fixed in advance, all three EN 71-3 material categories are potentially applicable and Method v2.0 step 3 requires the strictest applicable value: Category II carries the strictest limit set for every panel analyte, so it is the published ceiling. A specific article is never released to a looser category by intake classification; where its material form is Category I or Category III, the Category II ceiling published here still governs, which is deliberate over-compliance and is disclosed as such.
material: Determined per article at intake. Includes accessible liquids, gels, sticky and slime materials contained inside other toys.
components: Determined per article at intake and recorded in the certification file before testing. At minimum: every accessible homogeneous material, every applied coating, every liquid or gel fill, and every metal component, each as a separate test portion. Where the article maps onto an existing row, it is certified on that row instead and this row is not used.
basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III|II|I)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
basis_guard_note: This row's scope spans all three of the Directive's material categories at once — Category I (any dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material presented at intake), Category II (accessible liquids, gels, sticky fills, bubble solution and slime) and Category III (any scraped-off-type material presented at intake) — so the guard admits all three EU category rows and every applicable category row is named on each cell, letting the strictest bind rather than a single category label deciding the number. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum in the row's native basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; never occurrence-derived). Category 21 publishes on the element-migration basis only, pooling the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments, with each row pinned to the EN 71-3 material category or categories its scope actually spans.

Pb.basis: element MIGRATION from accessible toy material (EN 71-3, mg/kg of material) — the strictest of the three material-category limit sets this row's scope spans (Category II) is published across the whole row; a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum across the three material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 2.0 mg/kg for Category I, 0.5 mg/kg for Category II and 23 mg/kg for Category III, against 90 mg/kg under ASTM F963-17 and 90 mg/kg under both NOM-252-SSA1-2011 tiers. The Category II value binds at 0.5 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film; Canada SOR/2016-193, SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2018-83 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material, applied stickers and films, and accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings.Where the article is a toy intended to come into contact with food (play tea and dinner sets, play food, toy cooking and baking sets), Directive 2009/48/EC additionally requires it to satisfy food-contact law. Regulation (EU) 10/2011 sets specific migration into food far below anything in this row — lead not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, cadmium at 0.002, mercury and arsenic at 0.01, total chromium at 0.01, nickel 0.02, aluminium 1 — on a migration-into-food basis that is a third measured quantity. It is a companion obligation for food-contact toys and is never resolved into this cell. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans all three of the Directive's material categories and the strictest of them is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category I material (any dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material presented at intake) and Category III material (any scraped-off-type material presented at intake) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling; the compiled record's candidate set names every applicable category row with its value so the tag regulatory-alignment is read against the full disclosed set rather than as an assertion that Category II is this material's legal category. STRUCTURAL NOTE: the durable fix is to split this row into per-material-category sub-rows, each with its own basis and its own Directive category. That requires new Category 21 subcategory slugs in data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json, which is a Step 0 taxonomy lock and outside a remediation pass; it is recorded as an outstanding item rather than performed here.

tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total arsenic-migration maximum across the three material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 3.8 mg/kg for Category I, 0.9 mg/kg for Category II and 47 mg/kg for Category III, against 25 mg/kg under ASTM F963-17 and 25 mg/kg under both NOM-252-SSA1-2011 tiers. The Category II value binds at 0.9 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
tAs.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. The register row's own notes record only that the values are unchanged across F963-08/-11/-16/-17/-23. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a figure made mandatory by CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. If ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 / 8.3 is later ingested as a source page that quotes the conformity-decision rule and it does specify a correction, the question may be reopened on that record; until then the stricter figure binds, which is also the position already published on wiki/regulations/astm-f963-soluble-migration and wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. On this row the ASTM and NOM-252 arsenic figures (25 mg/kg) are looser than the binding Category II value of 0.9 mg/kg and do not change the ceiling; they are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family. Arsenic is limited as the TOTAL element by every instrument in the family; inorganic arsenic has no migration counterpart and is handled on the iAs cell. iAs.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in a toy or craft material whose form is determined case by case is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
iAs.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (arsenic, total element, both scope tiers), mandatory in Mexico since 2012-08-13. None of the four speciates arsenic.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. a toy or craft material whose form is determined case by case carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, NOM-252-SSA1-2011, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (mercury, total element, both scope tiers). None speciates mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Ni.label: Strictest applicable sovereign nickel-migration maximum across the three material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 75 mg/kg for Category I, 18.8 mg/kg for Category II and 930 mg/kg for Category III. The Category II value binds at 18.8 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans all three of the Directive's material categories and the strictest of them is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category I material (any dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material presented at intake) and Category III material (any scraped-off-type material presented at intake) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling; the compiled record's candidate set names every applicable category row with its value so the tag regulatory-alignment is read against the full disclosed set rather than as an assertion that Category II is this material's legal category. Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 3 750 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's liquid or sticky (Category II) material that is 0.2 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive TOTAL-tin migration maximum, strictest across the three material categories this row's scope spans (Category I 15 000, Category II 3 750 binding, Category III 180 000 mg/kg), recorded as a SCREEN; the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling for Category II material, 0.2 mg/kg, is a binding parallel obligation pending register ingestion.
Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 0.2 mg/kg for this row's liquid or sticky (Category II) material while this cell publishes 3 750 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans all three of the Directive's material categories and the strictest of them is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category I material (any dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material presented at intake) and Category III material (any scraped-off-type material presented at intake) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling; the compiled record's candidate set names every applicable category row with its value so the tag regulatory-alignment is read against the full disclosed set rather than as an assertion that Category II is this material's legal category. Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.basis: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category II (liquid or sticky material) value, the strictest of the three category values this row's scope spans; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element.
